_doc: Hot-path ids for `// perf-hot: <budget> <path-id>` markers (plans/cmux-next/codebase-health.md section 6). scripts/cmux-next/guardrails.py warns when a push changes a marked function and names the bench here. Run it yourself on the fleet (nx-remote --needs gui), light and STRESS (perf-lead-brief), before and after; never add it to CI.

cef-host-input.what: one input event forwarded to the Chromium host app (prototype, browserHost.helper): encode and one non-blocking write

cef-host-control.what: one control op to the Chromium host (ChromiumHostControlChannel.send): encode, then one non-blocking sendmsg or an outbox push (the reader flushes waiting frames in batches, one sendmsg each)
cef-host-control.bench: CMUX_CHROMIUM_HOST_CONTROL_BENCH=1 swift test --filter ChromiumHostControlSendBench (send p50/p95/p99/max, direct write and outbox push; Debug: the channel is Debug-only), on macOS 26 and 27

key-dispatch.what: every key-down: shortcut table, chord tracker, focus routing

terminal-key.what: terminal key to committed frame (input write, echo, parse, draw)

palette-key.what: Command Palette open and each query key to its first painted frame

omnibar-key.bench: scripts/cmux-next/omnibar-click-bench.py (focus), then bench-typing.py with the omnibar focused

motion-frame.bench: scripts/cmux-next/motion-main-work.py --vdisplay 120 (counts: RenderStats frame_sets, layouts, window_calls, tracking_area_adds in frames 2..n, light and STRESS), then scripts/cmux-next/motion-hitches.py (time: main ms per spring frame and hitches, RenderStats disarmed); scripts/measure/split-spring.sh --suite=pane-bench (PaneMotionBench, PaneMotionWorkTests), pane-perf-terminal.py and anim-perf-terminal.py stay for the panes.* rows

frame-tick.what: the per-display-frame delivery to every active frame client

drag-frame.what: one tab, pane or column drag frame (ghost, autoscroll, hit test)

cef-geometry.what: Chromium page geometry, clip and occlusion updates
cef-geometry.bench: scripts/cmux-next/pane-perf-terminal.py with a Chromium page (debug.cef geometry posts per frame)

cmd-tab.what: app activation (Cmd-Tab back): become/resign key notices to committed frame, including the hover refresh

new-tab.what: new terminal or Chromium tab to its first frame

action-perform.what: every ActionRegistry.perform turn's oracle hook: one nil check of the registry's immutable turnObserver (Release), or the depth count and one ActionRunObserver call at the end of the outermost turn (DEV, bench)
action-perform.bench: scripts/cmux-next/action-perform-ab.py run --base BASE_SHA --head HEAD_SHA (ActionPerformBench at both SHAs alternately on one host: what Release adds over the base per perform, 95% interval over paired runs), and CMUX_ORACLE_TURNS_BENCH=1 swift test -c release -Xswiftc -DCMUX_BENCH_HOOKS --filter OracleActionTurnsBench (the disarmed OracleActionTurns against no observer, interleaved rounds), on macOS 26 and 27

action-budget.what: every action run's always-on budget record: two clock reads and one ring-slot write (ActionBudgetMonitor.record)
action-budget.bench: CMUX_ACTION_BUDGET_BENCH=1 swift test -c release --filter ActionBudgetMonitorBench (ns per run and per batch), on macOS 26 and 27

main-task-ledger.what: every scheduled main-thread task's MainOwnerLedger slot: five relaxed atomic stores and a releasing store (MainOwnerLedger.ended)
main-task-ledger.bench: swift test -c release --filter MainOwnerLedgerTests/aLedgerWriteCostsUnderItsBudget (ns per slot write and per full-ring call; the whole posted run: MainTaskBoardSpanTests/aPostedTaskWithItsLedgerSlotCostsNanoseconds), on macOS 26 and 27

trace-ring-write.what: one Release trace ring record under a catalog id (TraceRing.write(name:)): the thread's TLS state, one acquire load of the active ring, the seqlock publish, a chunk claim every 31st record
trace-ring-write.bench: swift test -c release --filter 'TraceRingTests.*eightContendedThreadsKeepTheSingleThreadP99' (31-record batch p99, 1 and 8 threads)

trace-ring-write-interned.what: one trace ring record under a run-time name (TraceRing.write(_ InternedName)): the catalog-id write plus one relaxed load and a tag compare after the name's first record in the ring
trace-ring-write-interned.bench: swift test -c release --filter 'TraceNamesTests.*internedWriteCost' (31-record batch p50, interned vs catalog id)

main-turn.what: the always-on main run-loop turn meter: its four observer callouts per turn, the sendEvent input span and each scheduled task's span (MainTurnMeter, CmuxApplication.sendEvent); budget < 100 ns per turn over the clock reads
main-turn.bench: CMUX_MAIN_TURN_BENCH=1 swift test -c release --filter MainTurnMeterBench (ns per turn), on macOS 26 and 27

idle-energy-wake.what: the idle wakeup histogram's afterWaiting observer at every main run-loop wake (IdleEnergyMonitor.noteWake, debug.energy idle): one uptime read, one relaxed input-count load and a compare; one proc_pid_rusage read only when a window opens or closes; budget < 100 ns per wake over the uptime read
idle-energy-wake.bench: CMUX_IDLE_ENERGY_BENCH=1 swift test -c release --filter IdleEnergyMonitorBench (ns per wake, ns per rusage read), on macOS 26 and 27

terminal-feed.what: one terminal output chunk parsed on its TerminalOutputLane (ghostty_surface_process_output, microseconds for an echoed key, about 1 ms for 256 KiB) inside its terminal.feed hang scope (HangWatch.watch: two stores and no system call once p09-observability-066 fills the slots)
terminal-feed.bench: scripts/cmux-next/bench-typing.py (echo: output parsed stage p95); the scope's own cost: swift test -c release --filter HangWatchTests (p09-observability-066 open and close cost)

daemon-request.what: every daemon request and connection frame, key input included: the request watchdog's slot claim, clock read and release (cmux-tui-core server/request_watchdog.rs begin and RequestScope end)
daemon-request.bench: cargo test -p cmux-tui-core --release --lib -- request_watchdog_begin_bench --ignored --nocapture (ns per run), then scripts/cmux-next/bench-typing.py

resize-drag.what: one divider, column-edge, row-edge, sidebar-edge or DevTools-divider drag event and each coalesced delivery it gets (feature pointerFrameDrags: at most a leading and a trailing delivery per frame, PointerFrameCoalescer)
resize-drag.bench: scripts/cmux-next/divider-drag-reflow-live.py --tag TAG --out DIR with CMUX_ENABLE_FEATURES=pointerFrameDrags and without (frame intervals, drawn-grid lag), light and STRESS; swift test --filter 'DividerDragTests|SidebarResizeHandleTests' for deliveries per frame

terminal-pointer.what: one pointer move, drag or scroll event over a terminal and each coalesced delivery it gets (feature terminalPointerFrames: at most a leading and a trailing ghostty_surface_mouse_pos or mouse-reporting ghostty_surface_mouse_scroll per frame, PointerFrameCoalescer)
terminal-pointer.bench: swift test --filter 'TerminalPointerCoalescingTests' for Ghostty calls per frame; live: scripts/cmux-next/pointer-probe.swift path/drag (1000 Hz moves) over a terminal running a mouse-reporting program (vim with mouse=a), with CMUX_ENABLE_FEATURES=terminalPointerFrames and without, light and STRESS, reading ghostty.lock_wait and main stalls from debug.hangs
